rv.q: Grogan is a wonderfully watchable actor – you don't dare look away for fear of missing another flash of a breakdown.
It’s a cleverly stacked story in which each new block is as unexpected as the last.
You’re So Special proves that Julia Grogan certainly is.
Very much a case of ‘the kids are all right’, this case study of self-absorption in an individualistic society was quite intriguing.
The writing is punchy, effortlessly swinging between laugh out loud lines and disturbingly dark moments, and Grogan’s performance, directed by Rachel Lemon , is outstanding.
As it stands, this is a deft, theatrical and utterly contemporary story that delivers its promise with a spectacularly deranged finale, and calls into question our obsession with talent.
The dense, disheartening centre of a play about self-delusion and fame is well-balanced with its pleasingly unusual premise.
The dramatic soundtrack gives the play a Fleabag-esque vibe, strengthened by some of the crude language and themes.
Yet uneven writing, confusing direction and a collection of theatrical ideas that never form a coherent whole leave the piece frustratingly out of reach.

cn.t: Grogan's darkly comic one-woman show about a delusional baby ballet teacher desperate for fame earns strong praise for its sharp satire of artistic ambition, though some find the unhinged premise requires a generous suspension of disbelief.
